Sport Comeback Kings

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):


Unique Selling Point:
Background
The story explores the inspiring comeback stories of two South African sports icons, Chad Le Clos and Wayde van Niekerk. Both athletes faced significant challenges, including mental health struggles and injuries, as they embarked on their journeys to reclaim their positions as champions in the world of swimming and athletics.
II. Overview of Chad Le Clos's Comeback:
Title Segment: "From the Depths to the Podium"
Struggling to Make the Perfect Comeback:
, delve into Chad Le Clos's struggles and challenges in making a comeback in competitive swimming.
Highlight the hurdles he faced, both in and out of the pool, including his battle with suicidal thoughts and the importance of therapy in his recovery
The Road to Redemption:
Explore Chad Le Clos's determination to return to the podium, discussing his aspirations for the Paris 2024 Olympics.
Showcase how he overcame setbacks and his commitment to reaching the zenith of his swimming career.
III. Wayde van Niekerk's Journey Back to Glory:
Title Segment: "Sprinting through Adversity"
Injury, Recovery, and Ambition:
Discuss Wayde van Niekerk's remarkable recovery from a career-threatening injury, drawing insights from the articles.
Highlight the challenges he faced during rehabilitation and the mental resilience required to return to competitive sprinting.
Champion's Mindset:
Explore Wayde van Niekerk's mindset and determination to reclaim his status as the fastest man in the world.
Include details thar shed light on his preparations and goals for future competitions, showcasing his commitment to excellence.
IV. Unveiling the Human Side:
Title Segment: "Behind the Goggles and Starting Blocks"
Personal Interviews:
Conduct exclusive interviews with Chad Le Clos and Wayde van Niekerk to uncover their personal experiences, emotions, and reflections on their comeback journeys.
Use personal anecdotes and revelations to humanize the athletes and connect with the audience on a deeper level.
Impact on the Sporting World:
Explore the impact of these comeback stories on the world of sports, shedding light on the broader conversation around mental health in athletics.
V. Conclusion:
Title Segment: "Rising from the Depths"
Final Triumphs:
Conclude the documentary by showcasing Chad Le Clos and Wayde van Niekerk's ultimate triumphs on the global stage.
Emphasize the broader message of resilience, determination, and the ability to overcome adversity, inspiring viewers to face their challenges head-on.
VI. Production Plan:
Cinematography:
Capture visually stunning footage of the athletes in training, competitions, and personal moments.
Utilize a mix of archival footage and behind-the-scenes shots to create a dynamic visual narrative.
Narration and Interviews:
Engage a compelling narrator to guide the audience through the athletes' stories.
Include in-depth interviews with Chad Le Clos, Wayde van Niekerk, coaches, and relevant experts.


Extra Budget Items:
Flighta to Durban and Accommodation, as well as Car hire.

Script:


Script: Comeback King
Opening Sequence: Slow-motion visuals of Chad dropping the South African flag, getting ready: fast flashback 2012 race (under stirring music).
Upsound Chad le Clos 44:27 I just love to win….
Upsound Chad le Clos 24:20…. It's that moment of being King of the World.
Upsound Chad Le Clos 09:56 Never judge a man's character for how he celebrates victory…You judge him for when his back's against the wall.
Upsound Cha le Clos 37: 03 Even in my darkest hour, there was stil a small beat that just kept me going. [Sound effect of slow heartbeat]
Upsound Chad Le Clos 06:20: I have unfinished business…[dip to black after dive]
1. V/O Every four years, athletes from around the world converge to take part in The Olympic Games. Over 15,000 athletes from more than 200 countries compete to turn lifelong dreams into reality - for themselves, for their countries.
Link Xola: Becoming an Olympian or World Champion requires hours of dedication and hard work. Sometimes it means having to step away from the sport that you love to make the ultimate comeback.
2.V/O It’s an early Saturday morning in Pietermaritzburg, KZN, and we’re joining Olympic gold medal swimmer and former world record holder, Chad Le Clos, on a training session. He’s preparing for the next games in Paris later this year, and it’s a rare opportunity to see the dedication demanded of top athletes.
Upsound Xola: Wow Chad this is incredible commitment, what time do you usually get up?
Upsound Chad: I am always up before dawn.
Upsound Xola: That is a lot of dedication…Is this the comeback?
Upsound Chad: I am back baby, Lets get it.
Upsound Chad Le Clos: 12:20 When I close my eyes at night, I can't help but think about the Olympic GamesI want to make sure that I'm at my best next year at the Olympic Games and ah - fourth Olympics and hopefully bring back another medal, or two….

3.V/O With four Olympic medals to his name, Chad is our country’s most decorated swimmer… but his hopes of adding to that tally and to his reputation suffered a blow at the 2021 Games in Tokyo, Japan. He couldn’t crack a podium finish, and returned home without a single medal. It was the beginning of what he now considers the darkest period of his life.
4. V/O: This year’s Olympics in the French capital offers a chance at redemption; a chance for Chad to regain his rightful place among the sport’s greats.
Upsound Xola: 05:46 This comeback trail. How difficult is it? Or is it because your mind is in the right place that it's only natural, makes sense, and an easy transition?
Upsound Chad: 06: 36 I have unfinished business that I wanna do. You know, I wanna go down as one of the greats. I really want my name to be remembered in 20 years. I want them to say. I want them to put me up there with the Phelpses, with the Mark Spitzes, with Ian Thorpe.
Chad: 0When I finally hang up the goggles, I want it to be, he is number one.
[breather/transition]
5.V/O Chad first stunned the world by winning Olympic gold and silver at the 2012 Games in London at just 19. The highlight, an incredible 200m butterfly race, in which American swimming legend Michael Phelps was the hot favourite.
Upsound Chad 03:40 if I'm being honest with you. But I think destiny was calling that day. It was everything that I had dreamed of as a kid.
6.V/O Chasing his 15th Olympic title, Phelps led for the first 150 meters, significantly ahead of Chad.
Upsound Chad 02:43 When I was swimming in that race, I thought I was Michael Phelps…
7.V/O In third place on the final turn, things weren’t looking good for Chad. But he rallied to close the gap on the American....
8.V/O And with just 5 meters to go, the unthinkable happened.
Upsound Chad 02:43 I beat him at his own game. I was the only person in history still to this day to have ever beaten him in his own game, [breather using Bert visual of unbelievable]]
9.V/O With his advisor and biggest fan- his dad, proudly watching on... a South African hero was born.
10.V/O As a child, Chad first battled a deep-seated fear of water before starting swimming at the age of ten. His father Bert was his first coach.
Upsound Xola and Bert le Clos 00:21 Bert is life still unbelievable ? You had to get young Chad out to the swimming pool as a youngster. Didn't like it. Balled his eyes out.
Upsound Bert: Yes.
Upsound Xola I'm pretty sure at that stage you weren't thinking, this kid has got a long future swimming.
Upsound Bert Le Clos 03: 46 What are you talking about? He was playing soccer. Soccer was his first love. He was playing soccer, He never touched the ball. 05:45 I said, my boy, I don't want to tell you, but the reality of it all is you're a better swimmer than you are a soccer player.
11.V/O Recognizing his Olympic potential at just 14 when he secured a spot on the country’s senior national team, Chad’s mom, Gerry, quit her job to fully support his journey.
Unsound 03:31 [Xola] It is a full-time job, yeah. Yeah, being an Olympic mom. He was very young, Chad, when he took the world by storm.. He was world champs at 19, Olympics at 20.
Upsound Gerry 04:01 I had a nine to five job, but it just you know got out of hand so you know you need Chad needs a structure around him where he has to concentrate on swimming. I do the paperwork and Burt does other stuff.
[bridge, visuals of Chad practicing]
12. V/O Getting to the games - then …and now… means a rigorous training regimen, with extended hours in the pool and focused strength exercises. His routines involve precise technique drills, endurance laps, and specialized workouts, all aimed at optimizing speed and stamina.
13 V/O Now based in Frankfurt, Germany, and with a new coach, he’s not leaving anything to chance.
Upsound Chad 17:26 it comes down to taking care of your body. I sometimes forget that I am 31 and I want to still train at that high level of intensity every day with these youngsters but unfortunately, I actually can't keep that going I've got to be smart with my recovery and the way that I approach things.
14.V/O Being an Olympian extends beyond the physical; it's about navigating pressure and shouldering the weight of expectations. After his disappointing Olympic showing in Tokyo, Chad battled psychological demons.
Upsound Chad 39: 17 The worst time for me was definitely after the Olympics…I'll tell you, this is the truth. I was completely depressed A because I got fifth and I was like, should have medaled.
Upsound Chad 33:23 : No one's going to know the demons that I had to fight They're just going to see the results.
15 V/O He sunk deeper and deeper into depression and soon was spiraling out of control.
Upsound Chad 41:14 Three days before the World Championship// 40:48 I went to a party three, four days before, because I had to. I told my dad this. I said, I have to. When I got completely wasted, completely wasted, I just had to numb myself from life. // 41:14 that's the sad reality of where I was at that stage.
Upsound Chad 41:37 : It was just bad results really. Just bad results, that's all it was. It just wasn't me on top of the podium or in the medal stage.
Upsound Gerry 06 :05 : it's the hardest thing as a parent to see your child unhappy or suffering or in whatever situation.// 07:39 going through some mental health issues was tough on the family. 07 :49 Bert kept on telling him, Chad, phone the psychologist, phone the psychologist. And you need to do that sooner rather than later.
16 V/O Chad finally sought the professional help he needed, undergoing months of intensive therapy.
Upsound Bert 15:31 :I said, you know, Chad, I'm so flippin' proud of you because you've evolved. You're becoming a man because of your attitude to a problem.
Upsound Chad 35:08 My dad always just taught me, you know, just... Never give up. Put your head down and give your best.
Upsound Chad 36:05It took a lot of..a lot of psychology Its was just a tough time for me. Got right, thankfully, and I think I started to see that the results and the pool would get better also.I remember saying hey, in one year from now, I'm going to be a World Champion, double World Champion, in this race
[ Transition/breather Visuals]
17 V/O While Olympic gold remains a priority, he’s passionate about his work with the Chad Le Clos Foundation, teaching swimming and water safety to underprivileged communities… It also supports aspiring young swimmers in KZN.
Upsound Xola 46:28: . What is the foundation all about?
Upsoud Chad 47:10 Iwe have the highest.deaths from drowning. Can you believe that in the world? So my goal is to teach water safety. My goal is to help the intermediate swimmers break into that first team 47:25I. We have three and a half thousand. I believe 10,000 is easily achievable by the next Olympic cycle...

18 V/O After losing his way in 2021 he bounced back with an incredible performance at the 2022 World Championships in Melbourne, Australia, where, against all odds, he won gold in both the 100 and 200 meters butterfly.
19 )With the Paris Olympics just months away, Chad is ready to secure his legacy in what could be one of the most remarkable sporting comebacks ever.
Upsound Chad 24:15 It's that moment of being King of the World, you know? On top of the podium, hearing the anthem, putting your medal on, and with the flag. There's nothing better than that, you know? I can tell you honestly, that's the drug I'm chasing still. 12 years later.
[ end}







21 V/O After his upset in 2021 he bounced back with an incredible performance at the 2022 World Swimming Championships in Melbourne, Australia.
With the highly anticipated Olympic games just months away, Chad is ready to secure his legacy in what could be one of the most remarkable sporting comebacks ever.
[end]

Since the very beginning of his career, he is known because of his extraordinary wins and performances. He makes in the list of legendary swimmers after giving a shocking performance in the 200m
butterfly at London 2012. In this event, he made his way to the finals and was lined aup against legend Michael Phelps

Clos shocked the entire swimming community by grabbing gold from the all-time favorite Phelps in the 200m butterfly. He nabbed the win in the dying seconds and touched the wall just 0.05 seconds before the American swimmer.


V/O











Le Clos was on a comeback mission after he surrendered his title to Hungarian swimmer Laszlo Cseh in Kazan, Russia two years ago. To compound his disappointment Le Clos failed to defend his 200m butterfly title missing out on a podium place altogether at the Rio Olympic Games.

The South African prodigy Chad le Clos has always been on the top of what he does. Since the very beginning of his career, he is known because of his extraordinary wins and performances. He makes in the list of legendary swimmers after giving a shocking performance in the 200m
butterfly at London 2012. In this event, he made his way to the finals and was lined aup against legend Michael Phelps

Clos shocked the entire swimming community by grabbing gold from the all-time favorite Phelps in the 200m butterfly. He nabbed the win in the dying seconds and touched the wall just 0.05 seconds before the American swimmer.
Following his injury, it has been rather a bumpy ride for the South African swimming sensation Chad le Clos to perform at his level best. He is one of the most decorated Olympians and looks forward to the 2024 Paris Olympics.
The 31-year-old star swimmer failed to make it onto the podium in Tokyo 2020 (in 2021) and has been battling with niggling injuries and illness since the global showpiece.

Le Clos said he would be targeting a return to the podium in Paris 2024 in what would be his fourth Olympic appearance if he qualifies. Should he win silverware next year he would be the first South African to do so eight years apart.
Le Clos pulled out of this year’s World Long-Course Championships citing an illness that plagued him for four months

The illness came at a time when Le Clos seemed to have found some of his old sparkle including solid performances on the 2022 World Cup circuit where he won nine medals – five gold and four silver – to finish third overall in the men’s competition.
V/O Achieving Olympic Gold demands unmatched dedication… and hard work that goes beyond the capabilities of most.
He backed that up winning the 100-200m butterfly golden double at the 2022 World Swimming Championships (25m) in Melbourne. Highlighting his return to form he broke his own African Record in the 200m butterfly.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Background The story explores the inspiring comeback stories of two South African sports icons, Chad Le Clos and Wayde van Niekerk. Both athletes faced significant challenges, including mental health struggles and injuries, as they embarked on their journeys to reclaim their positions as champions in the world of swimming and athletics. II. Overview of Chad Le Clos's Comeback: Title Segment: "From the Depths to the Podium" Struggling to Make the Perfect Comeback: , delve into Chad Le Clos's struggles and challenges in making a comeback in competitive swimming. Highlight the hurdles he faced, both in and out of the pool, including his battle with suicidal thoughts and the importance of therapy in his recovery The Road to Redemption: Explore Chad Le Clos's determination to return to the podium, discussing his aspirations for the Paris 2024 Olympics. Showcase how he overcame setbacks and his commitment to reaching the zenith of his swimming career. III. Wayde van Niekerk's Journey Back to Glory: Title Segment: "Sprinting through Adversity" Injury, Recovery, and Ambition: Discuss Wayde van Niekerk's remarkable recovery from a career-threatening injury, drawing insights from the articles. Highlight the challenges he faced during rehabilitation and the mental resilience required to return to competitive sprinting. Champion's Mindset: Explore Wayde van Niekerk's mindset and determination to reclaim his status as the fastest man in the world. Include details thar shed light on his preparations and goals for future competitions, showcasing his commitment to excellence. IV. Unveiling the Human Side: Title Segment: "Behind the Goggles and Starting Blocks" Personal Interviews: Conduct exclusive interviews with Chad Le Clos and Wayde van Niekerk to uncover their personal experiences, emotions, and reflections on their comeback journeys. Use personal anecdotes and revelations to humanize the athletes and connect with the audience on a deeper level. Impact on the Sporting World: Explore the impact of these comeback stories on the world of sports, shedding light on the broader conversation around mental health in athletics. V. Conclusion: Title Segment: "Rising from the Depths" Final Triumphs: Conclude the documentary by showcasing Chad Le Clos and Wayde van Niekerk's ultimate triumphs on the global stage. Emphasize the broader message of resilience, determination, and the ability to overcome adversity, inspiring viewers to face their challenges head-on. VI. Utilize a mix of archival footage and behind-the-scenes shots to create a dynamic visual narrative. Narration and Interviews: Engage a compelling narrator to guide the audience through the athletes' stories. Include in-depth interviews with Chad Le Clos, Wayde van Niekerk, coaches, and relevant experts.
